items.title: Edmonton Elks defeat Montreal Alouettes to capture 113th Grey Cup
items.summary_auto: The Edmonton Elks are Grey Cup champions for the 15th time in franchise history. Led by quarterback Cody Fajardo's four total touchdowns, two passing and two rushing, the Elks hung on to defeat the Montreal Alouettes 37-30 at McMahon Stadium in Calgary on Sunday.

items.title: Snowbirds bid farewell to legendary jets in final flight over Calgary
items.summary_auto: The legendary CT-114 Tutor jets of the Canadian Forces Snowbirds took to the skies one last time over Calgary's McMahon Stadium Nov. 15, 2026, right before the 113th Grey Cup kicked off, setting the stage for a dynamic match between the Edmonton Elks and Montreal Alouettes.

items.title: Toronto Tempo earn No. 1 pick after winning 2027 WNBA draft lottery
items.summary_auto: The Toronto Tempo have won the WNBA Draft Lottery to pick first overall. University of Southern California guard JuJu Watkins is considered the top prospect in the 2027 draft class.

items.title: 'I cheated': South Korean admits he used AI to achieve top score in national exam
items.summary_auto: The marks attained by the top scorer on South Korea's national exam for aspiring tax accountants this year seemed too good to be true, and on ‌Sunday, skeptics were proven right when he confessed to using generative AI to cheat.

items.title: Community comes together to say farewell to Bailey, a dog with cancer
items.summary_auto: Dozens of neighbours met at a Dartmouth park to comfort the 12-year-old pet during one last outing. The CBC's Guiliana Grillo was there.

items.title: Steering issue caused tanker to crash into cruise boat, U.S. officials say
items.summary_auto: The asphalt tanker vessel that struck a docked paddlewheel cruise boat in the Mississippi River at ‌New Orleans on Friday experienced a steering problem in which its rudder was stuck in one position, U.S. transportation safety officials ​said on Sunday.

items.title: Nationwide flight grounding unlikely in Canada, says aviation expert
items.summary_auto: An aviation management expert says Canada is less likely than the United States to ground flights nationwide as that country did on Friday afternoon, calling the Canadian system a model its southern neighbours should look to.

items.title: Carney sets out to deepen ties with China. Has the threat landscape changed?
items.summary_auto: On the sidelines of the APEC summit this coming week, Prime Minister Mark Carney is set to meet with his Chinese counterpart, President Xi Jinping, in the hopes of deepening economic and trade ties.

items.title: TV providers say Rogers' Monday hockey move inflates prices, 'erodes' sports viewing
items.summary_auto: A trio of television providers are accusing Rogers Communications Inc. of violating competition rules and inflating Canadian sports fans' bills by moving Monday night hockey broadcasts exclusively to its Sportsnet Plus streaming service for this NHL season.

items.title: Russia will not compete at world junior hockey championship in Alberta, IIHF says
Satellite limitations imposed by Musk's SpaceX pose danger for Ukraine, Zelenskyy says
items.summary_auto: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy warned that limitations on the Starshield satellite system, operated by Elon Musk's SpaceX, could weaken defences around Ukraine's energy infrastructure ahead of the winter months, when Moscow has repeatedly targeted the power grid.

items.title: Carney pledges $560M to Brazil-led fund to protect rainforests
items.summary_auto: Canada has pledged up to $560 million over four years ​to protect rainforests as part of a project co-led by Brazil and Norway.

items.title: Trump breaks silence on FAA's nationwide ground stop, demands more money for air traffic control
items.summary_auto: U.S. President Donald Trump on Sunday broke his silence on the nationwide ground stop that snarled airline travel this weekend, using the incident to push Congress on money to fully upgrade the country's air traffic control system.

items.title: Fillier scores again as Canada tops Sweden, advances to face U.S. in women's hockey worlds final
items.summary_auto: Sarah Fillier continued her goal-scoring streak as Canada advanced to the world women's hockey championship gold-medal game with a 3-0 win over Sweden on Sunday. The United States shut out Finland 5-0 earlier in the day.

items.title: One person still missing after fishing boat capsized near Yale, B.C., search and rescue says
items.summary_auto: One person is still unaccounted for after a fishing boat reportedly capsized on the Fraser River in Yale, B.C., Friday afternoon. In a post to Facebook, Hope Volunteer Search and Rescue said the operation quickly turned into a search, after personnel were told there was another person in the water.

items.title: Rock & Roll Hall of Fame ceremony full of emotions as Phil Collins, Queen Latifah, more inducted
items.summary_auto: Saturday night's Rock & Roll Hall of Came ceremony brought out stars and emotional tributes as Phil Collins, Billy Idol, Luther Vandross, Wu-Tang Clan, Queen Latifah, Oasis, MC Lyte, Sade, Joy Division/New Order and Iron Maiden were inducted during the ceremony at the Peacock Theater in Los Angeles, along with producer Rick Rubin.

items.title: Carney, Quebec premier discuss U.S. trade, homelessness at first meeting in Cambodia
items.summary_auto: Premier Paul St-Pierre Plamondon said the meeting ended with federal support for the province's fight against homelessness, and the exchange of personal phone numbers. The premier also thanked the prime minister for his support of an economic summit that will take place in Quebec in 2027.

items.title: 'He lived and breathed it': NCAA football prospect from N.S. has died
items.summary_auto: A Nova Scotian who was set to play football at an American powerhouse college is being remembered for his exceptional talent and desire to get better on the field, but also his happy-go-lucky and teddy-bear nature off of it.

items.title: Carney cites her award-winning book on encampments. She's eyeing his plan to end homelessness
items.summary_auto: One of Canada's leading authors on homelessness says the prime minister’s plan to end it within 10 years is an "ambitious goal" that has potential, but won't actually go all the way.

items.title: Senior Hamas commander who helped oversee Oct. 7 attack killed in Israeli strike in Gaza
items.summary_auto: Hamas said on Sunday that a senior commander who helped plan and oversee the Oct. 7, 2023, attack on Israel had been killed in an Israeli airstrike, with the Israeli military confirming his death.

items.title: A hobby that pops: Saskatoon man's massive Coca-Cola collection inspired by rural roots
items.summary_auto: Jon Aschenbrener of Saskatoon estimates he has 5,000 to 10,000 items in his collection of Coca-Cola memorabilia, which began on the family farm northeast of Cupar, Sask.

items.title: It started with a lobster supper. Now it's an East Coast institution
items.summary_auto: The Shore Club in Hubbards, N.S., has spent more than eight decades serving up classic lobster suppers and live music to people from around the globe. A new CBC documentary pulls back the curtain on how the Harnish family managed to turn a rural dance hall into a Maritime institution.

items.title: A man was once murdered over the pronunciation of 'Newfoundland'
items.summary_auto: Newfoundlanders and Labradorians tend to feel strongly about the right way to pronounce the name of our island, but would you kill a man over it? In 1876, someone did.

items.title: Canada's health-care spending tops $10,000 per person this year. Where is the money going?
Scientists race to discover and protect what lives in the ocean
items.summary_auto: Scientists say not knowing what lives in our oceans holds back efforts to protect them. Marine biologists are racing to catalogue species — from carnivorous sponges to otherworldly sea slugs. Here's a closer look at the creatures hidden in our seas and how humans rely on them more than most realize.

items.title: Why researchers are using drones to keep polar bears and people apart
items.summary_auto: While studies have shown drone hazing to be effective on black bears, researchers are now trying to see if it works with polar bears — a bigger, more curious and more aggressive species. The goal is to adapt the technology to Canada's North and try to take some of the risk out of managing the bears.

items.title: English was the language I built my career in. In Canada, it became something to prove
items.summary_auto: Anusuya Datta had never given a second thought to knowing English, having always written and spoken in the language. After moving to Saskatchewan, people continually remarked on her English skills, both in complimentary and derogatory ways.

items.title: Facing 'uncomfortable' questions, King Charles shows the 'soft power' of the Crown
items.summary_auto: As with trips to Canada in 2025 and the United States earlier this year, King Charles's recent visit to the Caribbean saw him walking something of a diplomatic tightrope at a politically charged time. There seems to be an emerging pattern.

items.title: 3 months after mass entry, some 15,000 migrants remain in Ceuta
items.summary_auto: Three months after the mass entry into Ceuta, many migrants still hope the Spanish enclave will offer them a route to mainland Europe. Local authorities and residents are struggling with the surge.

items.title: Has treatment for stuttering been off base? New guidelines go beyond speech to the brain
items.summary_auto: More than 80 million people worldwide stutter, yet misconceptions on it persist in the medical field, and access to appropriate care can be limited. New international medical guidelines aim to change that.

items.title: Canada is spending more than ever on health care. Are we getting our money's worth?
items.summary_auto: Canada is spending more on health care than ever. Whether Canadians are getting more care for their money is another question. A new report from the Canadian Institute for Health Information (CIHI) projects health-care spending will reach a record $433 billion in 2026, or $10,398 per person, an increase of 4.8 per cent over last year.
